# Overlapping frequency polygons {#sec-overlapping-frequency-polygons}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_supersoaker(
    base_size = 15))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_supersoaker()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_supersoaker()`, modeled on a Super Soaker: neon orange plastic, a water blue plot area, neon green, purple, and blue marks, and an Arial Black title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1990)
soaker_shots <- tibble(
  shot_id = 1:600,
  model = rep(c("SS 50", "SS 100", "CPS 2000"), each = 200)) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("SS 50", "SS 100", "CPS 2000")),
         avg_range = c(`SS 50` = 25, `SS 100` = 35,
                       `CPS 2000` = 45)[as.character(model)],
         range_ft = round(rnorm(n(), mean = avg_range,
                                sd = 0.12 * avg_range), 1)) |>
  select(shot_id, model, range_ft)
labs_ovrlp_freq_poly <- labs(
  title = "Super Soaker range",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "200 shots from each model",
  x = "Range (feet)",
  color = "Model",
  linetype = "Model")
ggp2_ovrlp_freq_poly <- ggplot(data = soaker_shots,
       aes(x = range_ft)) +
  geom_freqpoly(aes(color = model, linetype = model),
    binwidth = 2, linewidth = 1)
ggp2_ovrlp_freq_poly +
  labs_ovrlp_freq_poly
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a categorical variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

::::

## Description

A [frequency polygon](frequency_polygons.qmd) shows where numbers fall, using points joined by straight lines. Overlapping frequency polygons do the same job as [overlapping histograms](overlapping_histograms.qmd): they let us compare the form the numbers take[^dist-shape] from one group to the next.[^groups] Instead of bars, each group gets its own line.

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_freq_poly
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

A Super Soaker is a big water gun. Every summer in the 1990s, water fights behind the house were won by the kid with the biggest Super Soaker. We'll make up[^simulate] 200 shots from each of three kinds of Super Soaker.[^models] Each kind gets its own mean for how far a shot goes (`avg_range`).[^range] A hill is a line that is high in the middle and low on both sides. `rnorm()` picks how far each shot goes from the hill that goes with its kind.[^normal] How far a shot usually falls from the mean is 12% of the mean,[^sd] so the shots from the stronger kinds land over more ground. Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same 600 shots every time you run the code below.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_freq_poly
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1990) # same 600 shots every time the code runs
soaker_shots <- tibble(
  shot_id = 1:600, # 600 different shots, one row each
  model = rep(c("SS 50", "SS 100", "CPS 2000"), each = 200) # 200 shots per model
  ) |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = c("SS 50", "SS 100", "CPS 2000")), # shortest to longest range
    avg_range = c(`SS 50` = 25, `SS 100` = 35, # average range in feet
                  `CPS 2000` = 45)[as.character(model)], # (looked up for each model)
    range_ft = round(
      rnorm(n(), mean = avg_range,
            sd = 0.12 * avg_range), # bigger soakers spread out more
      1 # one decimal place
      )
    ) |>
  select(shot_id, model, range_ft)
glimpse(soaker_shots)
```
:::

## Distribution

Overlapping frequency polygons make it easy to compare where each group stands on the `x` axis *and* how far from each other its numbers are.[^spread] In the shots we made up, both of those change together: a bigger Super Soaker sends water farther for the most part, and its shots land farther from each other. Below we'll move from the shots, to a graph, to the rule behind it.[^formula]

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first five shots (all from the SS 50).

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_freq_poly
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(soaker_shots, 5)
```
:::

These shots landed between about 22 and 26 feet. The numbers below[^summary] show that how far shots usually fall from the mean (`sd`) grows with the mean, but `sd` as a part of the mean (`cv`)[^cv] stays close to 0.12 for every kind.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_freq_poly
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
soaker_shots |> 
  group_by(model) |> 
  summarise(mean = mean(range_ft), sd = sd(range_ft), cv = sd / mean)
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The first graph below shows the three lines in feet. Each one stands farther to the right than the last, and each one is lower and wider. The second graph shows every shot as a part of the mean for its kind (a shot at the mean is 1),[^relative] which puts all three on the same number line. Once we do that, the three lines fall on top of each other, because they all have the same form.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_freq_poly
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(soaker_shots, aes(x = range_ft, color = model, linetype = model)) + 
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 2, linewidth = 1) + 
  labs(title = "Feet", x = "Range (feet)", color = "Model", 
    linetype = "Model")

soaker_shots |> 
  group_by(model) |> 
  mutate(relative_range = range_ft / mean(range_ft)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = relative_range, color = model, linetype = model)) + 
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 0.05, linewidth = 1) + 
  labs(title = "Relative to the average", 
    x = "Range / average range", color = "Model", linetype = "Model")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

Each kind's shots come from a [hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution)[^normal-dist] where how far shots usually fall from the mean is always the same part of the mean:

$$
X_m \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_m, \; 0.12\,\mu_m), \quad \mu = (25, 35, 45)
$$

Showing each shot as a part of the mean takes away the difference between the kinds: $X_m / \mu_m \sim \text{Normal}(1, 0.12)$ for every kind, which is why the lines in the second graph fall on top of each other. 12% of the mean is about 3 feet for the SS 50 but more than 5 feet for the CPS 2000, so the CPS 2000's line is wider and, with the same 200 shots, lower. Try giving every kind the same `sd` in `rnorm()` (say, 4 feet), and the three lines in the first graph will all be as wide as each other.


## Grammar


::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

  -   Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()`

  -   Start the graph with `ggplot()` and give it `data`

  -   Put `range_ft` on the `x` axis

  -   Give each `model` its own color and line *inside* `geom_freqpoly()`,[^linetype] and set `binwidth` to `2` and `linewidth` to `1`


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_freq_poly
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_ovrlp_freq_poly <- labs(
  title = "Super Soaker range",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "200 shots from each model",
  x = "Range (feet)",
  color = "Model",
  linetype = "Model")
ggp2_ovrlp_freq_poly <- ggplot(data = soaker_shots,
       aes(x = range_ft)) +
  geom_freqpoly(aes(color = model, linetype = model),
    binwidth = 2, linewidth = 1)
ggp2_ovrlp_freq_poly +
  labs_ovrlp_freq_poly
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_freq_poly
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_ovrlp_freq_poly <- labs(
  title = "Super Soaker range",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "200 shots from each model",
  x = "Range (feet)",
  color = "Model",
  linetype = "Model")
ggp2_ovrlp_freq_poly <- ggplot(data = soaker_shots,
       aes(x = range_ft)) +
  geom_freqpoly(aes(color = model, linetype = model),
    binwidth = 2, linewidth = 1)
ggp2_ovrlp_freq_poly +
  labs_ovrlp_freq_poly
```

[^dist-shape]: The shape of the variable's distribution.

[^groups]: The levels of a categorical variable.

[^packages]: Install and load the packages.

[^simulate]: Simulate.

[^models]: Three models: the SS 50, SS 100, and CPS 2000.

[^range]: The average range, in feet.

[^normal]: `rnorm()` draws values from a normal distribution with `mean = avg_range`.

[^sd]: The standard deviation is 12% of the mean (`sd = 0.12 * avg_range`).

[^seed]: Setting the random seed.

[^spread]: Where each distribution is centered *and* how spread out it is.

[^formula]: The formula.

[^summary]: Summary statistics.

[^cv]: The [coefficient of variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_variation), the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean.

[^relative]: Relative range: each shot divided by its model's average range.

[^normal-dist]: A normal distribution whose standard deviation is a fixed fraction of its mean.

[^labels]: Labels.

[^linetype]: Mapping `model` to both `color` and `linetype` keeps the groups apart in grayscale and for colorblind readers. Giving both the same title in `labs()` merges them into one legend.
